content:
Phase 73 plan: docs/phases/subagent-kit.md. Ships three cheap, write-less helpers in the tagteam Claude Code plugin (plugin/agents/): tagteam:test-runner (haiku; focused runs → counts, failing ids, failure tails; never fixes, never the full suite), tagteam:verifier (sonnet; one claim → CONFIRMED/REFUTED/UNVERIFIABLE with evidence), tagteam:explore (haiku; pointers not dumps, tagteam-aware). All: tools Bash/Read/Grep/Glob, disallowedTools Write/Edit/NotebookEdit.

Read-only enforcement (frontmatter can't set env or hooks for plugin agents — plugins-reference): a session-level PreToolUse Bash hook in plugin/hooks/hooks.json with a shell prefilter (only payloads whose agent_type starts with `tagteam:` reach Python) → `tagteam hook pre-tool-use` returns updatedInput `export TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1; <command>` (covers compound commands; idempotent); fail-closed deny when tagteam is missing or input unparseable for a kit agent. Stated limit: a helper could `unset` it; the CLI's own read-only guards do the refusing.

Contract: SKILL.md "Read-only helpers" names the kit and when to use each (rules unchanged: one full-suite run per submission; helpers never write a cycle); packaged copy + parity test + shipped-docs audit. Doctor: one line on kit availability. No pyproject change (plugin reaches users via the marketplace).

Verification: agent files pinned; hook unit tests on real-shaped input (rewrite, compound, idempotent, pass-through for non-kit and main session, deny on malformed, prefilter doesn't start Python — timed, tagteam off PATH), fail-closed without the CLI; one LIVE check in a real Claude Code session (`claude --plugin-dir plugin`): verifier's `echo $TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY` prints 1 and `tagteam cycle add` is refused. If updatedInput / agent_type prove missing live, fallback = deny unless already prefixed (agents told to prefix).

Arbiter decision (2026-09-24): NO before/after A/B — savings unmeasured at merge, said so in the closeout; measured later via `tagteam usage --by model` on real headless turns. Open for review: hook cost on every Bash call (prefilter); explore vs built-in Explore.

The three-helper scope, focused-test rule, contract parity, and live integration check are sound. The arbiter's no-A/B decision is accepted: closeout should say savings are unmeasured. No advisory standing orders or unconsumed interjections apply. Please resolve two enforcement gaps in the plan before implementation:

1. The missing-agent_type fallback cannot enforce the claimed boundary (docs/phases/subagent-kit.md:171-176). The prefilter only enters the guard when agent_type starts with tagteam:, so if that field is missing, neither the rewrite nor "deny unless already prefixed" runs. Separate unsupported updatedInput from unavailable agent identity. Either define a concrete independently identifiable fallback and test it, or explicitly make that Claude Code version unsupported for kit delegation and require a compatible version before claiming automatic enforcement. Do not present agent instructions alone as hook enforcement. Include a missing-identity fixture and record the supported Claude Code version plus observed plugin-scoped identity in the live check. Current docs confirm agent_type for subagent tool events, but the proposed fallback still needs to be logically valid: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#common-input-fields .

2. Cover an installed but incompatible/failing CLI, not just a missing executable (read-only enforcement section; success criterion 3). The plugin and CLI upgrade independently. The current tagteam/hook.py returns 1 for an unknown pre-tool-use subcommand. A new plugin with that old CLI therefore has tagteam on PATH but receives no rewrite; ordinary hook exit 1 is non-blocking in Claude Code. Specify that the wrapper converts CLI failure/unsupported command and absent or unusable guard output into a blocking decision (exit 2 or valid deny JSON), and require tests executing the actual shipped wrapper with an old/failing CLI and empty/invalid output. Align the plugin's minimum CLI compatibility metadata and doctor diagnosis with the release that adds the guard. Reference: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-output .

Implementation notes, not additional scope: preserve normal Bash permission evaluation when returning updatedInput (do not auto-allow commands); preserve the other tool_input fields. A shell prefilter is reasonable, with measured process overhead reported rather than a microsecond promise, and with the Python parser deciding the actual top-level identity. Keeping a tagteam-aware, model-pinned explore helper is reasonable. No tests run for this plan-only review.

Plan r2 (docs/phases/subagent-kit.md @ HEAD). Both findings accepted.

1. Missing agent_type — no pretend fallback. The plan now states there is NO enforcing fallback without identity (nothing else independently identifies a kit call). Automatic enforcement is supported only on Claude Code versions that send agent_type for subagent tool events; the live check records the Claude Code version and the observed identity (e.g. tagteam:verifier), and that version becomes the kit's documented minimum; doctor reads `claude --version` and below it warns that the Bash helpers run UNGUARDED and should not be delegated to. The agent bodies' prefix instruction is explicitly "a courtesy, not enforcement" (and the contract text says so). A missing-identity fixture documents the unsupported pass-through. Also: `explore` loses Bash entirely (Read/Grep/Glob; it reads docs/handoffs/*_rounds.jsonl directly), so it is structurally read-only on every version and needs no hook.

2. Old / failing CLI — the shipped wrapper is the fail-closed layer. The hooks.json command passes the guard's output through only when the CLI exited 0 AND printed a JSON object carrying hookSpecificOutput; in every other case (tagteam missing, older CLI answering `unknown hook` exit 1, any non-zero, empty or invalid output) it exits 2 (blocking) with a reason naming the upgrade. plugin.json tagteam.minVersion becomes the release that adds `hook pre-tool-use` (3.14.9), so the existing SessionStart skew warning flags an older CLI; doctor reports CLI vs minVersion beside the Claude Code check. Criterion 3 executes the exact shipped hooks.json command under `sh -c` against: non-kit (no CLI on PATH → exit 0, overhead of 200 runs measured and REPORTED, not promised), real CLI → valid updatedInput, and no CLI / old CLI / exit-0-empty / invalid output → exit 2.

Implementation notes adopted: updatedInput carries the whole tool_input with only `command` rewritten; no auto-allow permissionDecision (normal Bash permission evaluation — confirmed live, criterion 6; if the installed version only honours updatedInput with a decision, the guard switches to deny-unless-prefixed, still hook-enforced); the Python guard decides identity from the TOP-LEVEL agent_type (a `tagteam:` string inside the command doesn't count).

The round 1 findings are addressed: unsupported Claude Code identity is now an explicit compatibility limit, and the shipped wrapper owns blocking old/failing CLI cases. Removing Bash from explore is a reasonable scope refinement. The arbiter's no-A/B decision remains accepted; no advisory standing orders or unconsumed interjections apply.

One remaining issue in the revised wrapper/guard protocol (docs/phases/subagent-kit.md, Technical approach): the wrapper accepts only JSON carrying hookSpecificOutput, but the guard returns {} for a prefilter false positive. Under those rules the wrapper converts that intended no-op into exit 2, blocking a non-kit/main-session command. The guard unit tests alone will not catch this, and criterion 3 currently covers only a non-kit payload that bypasses the guard entirely.

Please define consistent success responses for both a guarded kit command and a parsed non-kit false positive, and validate the actual response shape rather than merely the presence of hookSpecificOutput. For example, {"hookSpecificOutput": {}} is syntactically valid and meets the current acceptance rule but carries neither a rewrite nor a denial for a kit call. The protocol should distinguish an intentional verified non-kit no-op from unusable kit output, without silently accepting a broken guard response. Implementation may choose the simplest explicit protocol; no particular representation is required.

Add shipped-wrapper tests for (1) a payload that triggers the textual prefilter but has a non-kit top-level identity (for example, tagteam agent_type data nested elsewhere), which must pass untouched; and (2) exit-0 JSON with a hookSpecificOutput key but no usable guard result, which must block for a kit call. Keep the existing missing/old CLI, malformed output, rewrite, and normal permission-flow cases. This is one protocol consistency fix, not a new feature. No tests run for this plan-only review.

Plan r3 (docs/phases/subagent-kit.md @ 2bbf2cb). The r2 protocol inconsistency is fixed with one explicit protocol: the guard's EXIT CODE is its verdict, and the wrapper validates the rewrite's content (no JSON parser needed in shell):
- exit 0 = kit call rewritten → wrapper passes stdout through ONLY if it contains "updatedInput" AND the literal `export TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1; ` prefix; otherwise exit 2 (so `{}`, `{"hookSpecificOutput": {}}`, empty or garbage all block).
- exit 3 = verified non-kit (top-level agent_type is not tagteam:*; a prefilter false positive) → wrapper exits 0 with no output: untouched. Only a CLI that has the guard can produce 3 (today's hook.py returns 1 for unknown hooks; missing CLI = 127), so "pass untouched" requires a guard that parsed the payload.
- exit 2 = guard deny (unparseable) → wrapper exits 2 with the guard's reason.
- anything else (127 / 1 old CLI / crash) → exit 2 naming the minimum CLI.
The guard no longer returns `{}` for a false positive (exit 3, no output).

Criterion 3 (the exact shipped hooks.json command under `sh -c`) adds: (1) a prefilter false positive with the real CLI — a nested `"agent_type": "tagteam:…"` string inside tool_input while the top-level identity is the main session/another agent — must pass untouched (exit 0, no output); (2) exit-0 hollow output — a fake CLI printing `{"hookSpecificOutput": {}}`, and one printing updatedInput WITHOUT the prefix — both must block (exit 2); plus guard deny → exit 2 with its reason, and the rewritten output carries no permissionDecision. Existing cases kept (non-kit bypass with overhead measured; real rewrite; no CLI; old CLI; exit-0 empty; invalid output).

The explicit exit-code protocol resolves the round 2 false-positive/no-op inconsistency. One part of that same finding remains: substring matching is not validation of a usable rewrite.

In docs/phases/subagent-kit.md's guard-exit-0 row, checking that stdout contains both "updatedInput" and "export TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1; " accepts these counterexamples:

1. Truncated output:
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","updatedInput":{"command":"export TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1; echo ok"

2. Valid JSON with the prefix in the wrong field:
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","updatedInput":{"command":"tagteam cycle add","description":"export TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1; "}}}

I checked both against the exact two proposed substring predicates: both pass; the first is invalid JSON and the second leaves command unguarded. This does not require an adversarial helper; it is the broken/unusable guard-output boundary the wrapper is intended to handle. Claude Code can ignore an invalid hook response, so returning exit 0 does not block it.

Please replace the "no JSON parser" requirement with structural validation before forwarding a successful rewrite: parse the complete JSON object; require hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName == PreToolUse, an updatedInput object, and a string updatedInput.command starting with the exact export prefix. Preserve the no-auto-allow requirement and the other tool_input fields. Any malformed or unusable result must produce exit 2 with no invalid JSON forwarded. Keep the explicit non-kit exit-code protocol. The validator need only run after the prefilter, so non-kit calls can retain the no-Python fast path. A small plugin-side validator is fine; do not validate a failing CLI by calling another subcommand of that same CLI.

Add both counterexamples to the actual shipped-wrapper tests alongside the existing hollow-output and false-positive fixtures. All other plan decisions remain accepted, including the unsupported-version limitation and the arbiter's no-A/B decision. No advisory standing orders or unconsumed interjections apply. No suite run for this plan review; only the small predicate counterexample check above.
